definitions.gloss: light brown sugar; sanontou (a Japanese sugar with a caramel-like color and flavor)
definitions.explanation: A Japanese type of brown sugar produced by repeatedly heating the sugar syrup that remains after white sugar is extracted. It is pale brown with a mild caramel flavor and is used widely in home cooking, especially for simmered dishes.

examples.japanese: ⟦{砂糖|さとう}→砂糖：00884_satou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{三温糖|さんおんとう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧。
examples.english: I use sanontou (light brown sugar) as my sugar.

examples.english: Adding sanontou gives simmered dishes a richer flavor.

examples.japanese: うち⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{白砂糖|しろざとう}→白砂糖：26404_shirozatou⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧{三温糖|さんおんとう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: At our house we use sanontou more often than white sugar.

notes:
Written with ⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧ (three), {温|おん} (warm, heat), and {糖|とう} (sugar). The name reflects the production process, in which the sugar syrup is heated three times, giving the sugar its characteristic caramel color and flavor.

Despite its appearance, {三温糖|さんおんとう} is not truly unrefined sugar — it is refined white sugar whose remaining syrup has been caramelized by repeated heating. It is especially popular in traditional Japanese cooking for ⟦{煮物|にもの}→煮物：04971_nimono⟧ (simmered dishes) and ⟦{照|て}り{焼|や}き→照り焼き：17668_teriyaki⟧.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {三温糖|さんおんとう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}う→使う：00473_tsukau⟧: to use sanontou
- {三温糖|さんおんとう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{加|くわ}える→加える：01941_kuwaeru⟧: to add sanontou
- {三温糖|さんおんとう}⟦{大|おお}さじ→大さじ：22527_oosaji⟧1: one tablespoon of sanontou

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{白砂糖|しろざとう}→白砂糖：26404_shirozatou⟧: white sugar — the most common refined sugar
- {黒砂糖|こくざとう}: unrefined brown/black sugar — darker and stronger-flavored
- ⟦グラニュー{糖|とう}→グラニュー糖：23996_guranyuutou⟧: granulated sugar — larger crystals, neutral flavor
- きび{砂糖|ざとう}: raw cane sugar — pale brown, less processed than sanontou
